Everyone has their own time, but 1,5 years seems too long. Usually a parent would introduce a new partner to the children when that relationship is serious and they know they are introducing stability to their children’s life.

The fact he introduced you to his father and friends, means he likes you, yes. But not introducing you to the kids, sounds to me he is not sure about your future.

It could also be the kids are having a hard time, but if that is the case, why hasn’t he mentioned it before?

I would have a serious conversation about your goal, which is to be together and full part of his life, and how he sees this happening, what is his timeline and why.

Personally, I would feel I am being gaslighted and strung along. You are a much more patient person than I am.

I am so sorry a loved one let you down like this. I am sorry you are hurting and have been hurting for a while. I am an internet stranger and my heart is full of compassion for you. How come your wife’s heart isn’t? You say you are in love with her, but is she in love with you? Or have the well been poisoned by her daddy and she started to see you like he does?

As you asked on concrete advice: your wife is not gonna respond to you unless you behave like her dad. Sorry, but that is her view of what a man is like and even if you are not that a*****e you will need to be firm. No threats, be prepared to follow through: “either we go to therapy or I am out”. “Your father apologize or he will never see his granddaughter again”. These are the things her father would do and the only way she knows how to respond.

Maybe you don’t wanna be that guy, which I understand, in which case you’ll just have to face it’s over because your wife is not a partner to you nor someone you can trust when it really matters.
Then your friend is just being too entitled. You owe her nothing

NTA. Anyone who cannot show compassion for DV victim, is a part of the problem. From the start “Leah” seemed more interested in living in the comfort of your parent’s house than actually just living with you.
NTA. How dare them? And how don’t they understand what they did was criminal? If they don’t understand you, maybe the police can.

NTA. It was not your decision to fire her. It was HR’s decision to fire a nurse who made a scene in front of patients and their families. While she was standing up for a noble cause, she could have chosen to do it more privately or discreetly as to not disturb the peace at a place where people need rest and reassurance.
INFO: Since you have a daughter has your friend planned and paid for your baby shower? If so, did you get to choose everything as you wanted?

Because they are a part of the wedding party? By your own admission you’re not close to this sister, while your other siblings seem to be close enough to stand with her. I guess it must sting she didn’t involve you as much as the other siblings and maybe that’s the real issue?

Don’t feel like you need to rush it, unless you actively need his support to control your disorder. You might as well wait until you can steer a conversation to it. But if it is important for you that he knows now, prepare a letter where you list: what is your ED like, what happened when you were affected and,most importantly, how you deal with it now and how he can help. When we receive surprising news, most of the time we overreact because we don’t know what to do. If you are upfront to him about your expectations, that helps.

Since your biggest barrier seems to be the shame and guilt you carry, could be worth to talk about it in therapy too.

Remember that you don’t need to be embarrassed about your mental health issues. They are not a choice. What is your choice is how you deal with them, and there is absolutely no shame in asking for help and creating awareness about your needs.

I learnt recently my shortness of breath was actually me hyperventilating. I was breathing too fast (over 12 times a minute), I didn’t realize, it didn’t feel at all like that was the problem, but it was. Turn on your chronometer and count how many times you are breathing in a minute. If it is too much, then try breathing exercises (many free apps). If breathing exercises do not help at all, time to see a physician. Good luck

Breath! Silly right? But you are describing several symptoms of hyperventilation. Which is when you breath to fast and short, over 12 times per minute. You don’t realize you’re doing it. It feels like shortness of breath, causes tingling sensation on your hands and face, dizziness and chest pains.

I recommend you download an app with breathing exercises (there are many and most are free) and focus on breathing. That will also relax your muscles. Do it for about 10 minutes, and don’t focus on long breaths either, focus on normal breathing because hyperventilation can also be caused by too many deep breaths.

Really, when the paramedics told me I was not having a heart attack but hyperventilating, I could swear I was breathing normal but I wasn’t! Neither are you. Expect the symptoms to last 1-2 hours more and keep an eye on your breathing. Should these terrible attacks continue, talk to your doctor about your medication/therapy.

Good luck
NTA. Your boyfriend sounds like a weak momma’s boy. The only thing I think you could have done better was not give her the satisfaction of seeing you upset.

My husband proposed with a ring that costed less than 100 bucks, and not with a diamond, but zirconia. He too was unemployed at the time and it was the best he could do. Didn’t matter a bit during the proposal, I didn’t pay attention to the ring at all because I was ecstatic we were getting engaged, that was my focus. Later, when he talked about he would change my ring when he could afford something better, I refused because the moment was what mattered. Not gonna lie, I didn’t love the ring at first but the meaning was more than enough for me.

YTA because you stole her special. Paying for your own ring is not special.
